# dsh-think-strip
**Keep DeepSeek Harness conversations alive for hundreds of turns without paying for the same reason
arness conversations alive for hundreds of turns without paying for the same reasoning text twice.**
This plugin strips historical **reasoning blocks** and **oversized tool outputs** out of the model's
context. Originals are archived to disk by timestamp with a searchable index; in their place the mo
del sees a one-line summary (for reasoning) or a head/tail preview plus the archive path (for tool r
a one-line summary (for reasoning) or a head/tail preview plus the archive path (for tool results).
Two per-session switches sit left of the chat composer — **thinking** and **tools** — and they are i
ndependent. New sessions follow configured defaults.
> Interface language: the plugin ships English and Chinese strings (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.jso
n`). Documentation: English · 中文
## What it guarantees
- **The append-only session log is never rewritten.** Originals stay in `session.v4.jsonl.zstd`, so

fork / resume / replay behave exactly as before.
- **Prompt-cache prefixes survive.** Stripping happ
ens mid-history, but once a strip is committed the message sequence is byte-stable, so prefix cachin

g keeps hitting.
- **Nothing is lost.** Each stripped item is written as its own JSON file, indexed
in `index.jsonl`, and the replacement text in context names the archive path — the model can go read
it when it actually needs the detail.
## How it works
Two cooperating channels, neither of which touches the log:
1. `appendPluginRecord(session, 'plugin:think-strip', { targets, indexed })` — writes one `ignorable

: true` plugin record. It never enters the surface nodes and survives a DSH restart.
2. `ctx.session
s.registerMessageProjection({ type: 'plugin:think-strip', project })` — registers the matching proje
ction. On fold, the `seq`s named by the record are replaced with **frozen copies** (each keeps its o
riginal `message.id`).
Each entry in `targets` is `{ seq, kind, summary?, replacement? }`, where `kind` is `'reasoning'` or
`'tool'`. **Records without a `kind` are read as `'reasoning'`**, so records written by v0.1 keep w
orking and old sessions do not break on upgrade.
Timing: on `agent/turn-stopping` (the turn is closing and the model owes no reply) the plugin rescan
s **all** history, archives originals first, then commits a single record covering every target `seq
**all** history, archives originals first, then commits a single record covering every target `seq`.
Rescanning everything rather than only the current turn matters: turns from before the plugin was en
abled — or before a switch was flipped — have accumulated originals that would otherwise sit in cont
ext forever. Already-processed messages come back from `session.deriveEventMessage(event)` without t
heir originals (the projection is applied), so they are skipped for free. `session.surface.nodes` do
ubles as a whitelist, skipping messages already hidden by compaction.
### Why not some other seam
| Candidate | Why it does not work |
| `agent/pre-step` to rewrite `messages` | That array holds only the user batch claimed for this ste

p; history is not in it (`dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:902-927`, `this.inbox.claim(...)`) |
| Surface
replace on `assistant/message` | Hard-rejected by the kernel: `assistant/message embeds its source

stream and cannot carry sourceEventSeqs` |
| `llm/stream` waterfall mutating `options.messages` | Th

e request is deep-frozen — "listeners read it, never rewrite it" |
| `agent/request` waterfall | Doc

umented as unable to mutate messages |
| Plain `session.append()` with a custom type | A normal appe

nd cannot set `ignorable`; reopening the session rejects unknown events |
| The built-in `tool-resul
t-pruner` | Broken in this DSH build: it reads `event.data.message.content[0].content` (assuming nes
ting) while the real shape is a flat `ContentBlock[]`, so `pruneContent(undefined)` throws. It is al
so `disabled: true` at `cordis.yml:321` |
## Caveats
- **The projection lives in the plugin.** Uninstalling it makes sessions that used it refuse to deri
ve further (`session message projection "plugin:think-strip" was removed or replaced`). To uninstall

, archive those sessions first or accept that they can no longer be opened.
- **One record per turn,

not per step.** Multiple steps in a turn are covered by the same record.
- **Tool results are only
processed when they are entirely `text` blocks.** Results containing images / files / structured blo
cks (32 of 1101 measured were `text,image`) are skipped whole — splitting image blocks risks more th

an it saves.
- **Content that fails to archive is not projected.** Those `seq`s stay in context with

a warning logged — better to spend the tokens than to lose the original.
- When compaction replaces
a span of history with a summary, the hidden `seq`s are no longer on the surface and the projection

silently skips them.
- **Plugin records must contain no `undefined` values.** `Session.append` vali
dates with `snapshotJsonValue`, which only accepts booleans / strings / finite numbers / plain objec
ts / plain arrays; a single `undefined` throws `session event "…" carries non-JSON-serializable data
` and the projection never commits (the archive is still written, but context is unchanged). Everyth
ing therefore goes through `toJsonSafe()` (`lib/pure.js`), which strips `undefined` keys via a JSON

round-trip.
- **Changing plugin source requires a DSH restart.** Modules under `node_modules` do not

participate in HMR; only config changes hot-apply.
- Lifecycle markers: `<archiveDir>/plugin.log` g
ets one line per `apply`; with `trace` on, each turn appends `turn=N sid=… sw=r1t1 ev=<events> sf=<s
urface nodes> targets=<hits> committed|targets=0|FAILED`, which separates "plugin never started" fro
m "started but never fired" from "fired but matched nothing" from "matched but failed to commit".
